message.content: {"answer": "B", "option_text": "Organizing pneumonia", "reason": "The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, patchy, peripheral airspace opacities (consolidations) that are non-segmental and migratory in appearance. This distribution is the classic radiological hallmark of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP). While bronchioloalveolar carcinoma can present similarly, the multifocal bilateral nature strongly favors OP. Sarcoidosis typically presents with hilar adenopathy and upper lobe reticulonodular patterns; Wegener's usually shows nodules/cavities; TB favors apical cavitation or consolidation; and lymphoma is less likely to present as acute bilateral peripheral consolidations."}
